### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerMetaItemHistoryRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via toVersion (literal, a string literal in registerMetaItemHistoryRoutes))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e77550d11215784259c9ba561309470561f2f3e8` — the merge of head `e03bd96c3a30d1b4efa2a4a81d196bf116f202a7` into base `b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e77550d11215784259c9ba561309470561f2f3e8 && git checkout e77550d11215784259c9ba561309470561f2f3e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e e03bd96c3a30d1b4efa2a4a81d196bf116f202a7 && git checkout -B drift-repro b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e && git merge --no-ff e03bd96c3a30d1b4efa2a4a81d196bf116f202a7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b8c959013b1ed5b9c6767994d3eb805b5c45b13e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e03bd96c3a30d1b4efa2a4a81d196bf116f202a7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-query-number-census.test.ts + packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`UNDECLARED_WHOLE_NUMBER_PARAM`, `readDeclaredQueryNumber`, `META_ITEM_ROLLBACK_PARAMS`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`rollbackItem`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`rollbackMetaItem`'s own guard), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`RollbackMetaItemResponseSchema`; no request schema), packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-query-multiplicity.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-query-number-reads.test.ts, packages/rest/package.json (zod `^4.6.5`), .objectui-sha (`6fb31dcc99`), .changeset/25482-rollback-to-version-integer.md (prose face, read for ②)

Diff read as `dc3e5b9d7b` (merge-base of `origin/main` and the head, the base the claim named) → `e03bd96c3a`, one commit, 3 files, +115 / −22. Card #25482 body and all three comments read (triage 6370228332, claim 6371817529, os-dev-report 6373954258). Check-runs on the head: 41, 34 `success`, 7 `skipped` (opt-in and main-only lanes), 0 failures; the five required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — all `success`; `Check Changeset` `success`. No governed path in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `POST /meta/:type/:name/rollback`, JSON body `toVersion` (and the `version` alias): FROM "whatever `Number()` makes finite and ≥ 1" TO "a JSON number that `z.number().int()` accepts and is ≥ 1" — right.** The hunk replaces `Number(body.toVersion ?? body.version ?? req.query?.toVersion)` with a body-first `safeParse` against `UNDECLARED_WHOLE_NUMBER_PARAM` (`z.number().int().optional()`, rest-server.ts:793) and keeps the door's own below-1 floor. Under zod 4 `z.number()` refuses non-numbers, `NaN` and non-finite values and `.int()` refuses fractions, so `true`, `[2]`, `"2"`, `1.5`, `"abc"`, `{}` all land on the existing `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, and `0` / `-1` on the kept floor. This is exactly the card's **Expected** line and the message the door already printed (`'toVersion' (positive integer) is required`). The spec declares only `RollbackMetaItemResponseSchema` (protocol.zod.ts:2189) and no request schema, so there is no declared contract the body judgement contradicts.
2. **`{"toVersion": 1.5}` moves from `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND` (forwarded to the protocol) to `400 INVALID_REQUEST` — right;** the card names this as the defect's third face, and the protocol's own guard (protocol.ts:29918, not finite or below 1) is untouched and now only ever sees a whole number.
3. **The `(narrowing)` arm — a numeric STRING in the JSON body (`"2"`) is now refused — right, and correctly declared.** The only in-repo sender is `@objectstack/client`'s `rollbackItem(type, name, toVersion: number, …)` (index.ts:2303), which sends `JSON.stringify({ toVersion })` with a typed number. A repo-wide grep at the head for a string-typed `toVersion` finds only package-version strings (`'2.0.0'`), `/diff` query tests, and one rollback test that sends `'4'` as a **query** value (member-selector test :253, which still passes through the reader). No doc under `content/docs`, `skills/` or `examples/` shows a string body. The claim's own `Basis for the Clause-② line` foresaw this revision ("revised with a narrowing arm if the measured diff refuses an input a real client sends"); the dev measured and revised. Right.
4. **`?toVersion=` is read through `readDeclaredQueryNumber(req.query, 'toVersion', UNDECLARED_WHOLE_NUMBER_PARAM, { emptyIsAbsent: false })` — right, and it introduces no NEW refusal on the query path.** Read against the reader (rest-server.ts:858–878): a blank value was `Number('') = 0` → refused before and is handed to the schema as `''` → refused now; `abc` → `NaN` → refused both before and now; `Infinity` → non-finite → refused both; `1.5` → forwarded before (then 404), refused now (right, see 2); absent → `.optional()` passes `undefined` → the door's own "required" `400`, as before; `3` → 3. `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` still runs first (multiplicity test :285 pins the two-value array by name), so the reader sees a single string, as its docblock requires. `/diff` reads its versions through the same declaration (`emptyIsAbsent: true` there, because `parseV('')` already meant absent on that door; `false` here, because `Number('')` already meant refused on this one) — the per-door empty judgement is applied as the reader's docblock prescribes.
5. **The reader's thrown `validationFailure` is caught by a bare `catch` and answered as the door's own `400 INVALID_REQUEST` instead of the `VALIDATION_FAILED` + `fields[]` envelope — right, by the card's ruling, with one note.** The card's Expected line and the triage ruling (6370228332) both prescribe `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; the deleted ledger row's own reason said moving this door onto `VALIDATION_FAILED` "would be a wire change to a door that already refuses, which no card here decides"; `#6877`'s multiplicity refusal on this door is unchanged. The only throw the reader makes is `validationFailure`, so the bare `catch` swallows nothing else. Note for the next card on this door: if it ever moves onto the data surface's `VALIDATION_FAILED` envelope, this `try`/`catch` goes with it (the reader docblock's default is to let `handleRouteError` answer).
6. **Precedence `toVersion` → `version` → `?toVersion=` is unchanged — right.** The old `??` chain skipped `undefined` and `null`; the new guard is `bodyVersion !== undefined && bodyVersion !== null`, the same two values. One consequence the body prose states correctly: a present-but-invalid body value (`"2"` beside `?toVersion=5`) is refused rather than falling through to the query — "judged as it came". Pinned by the precedence test.
7. **No public export, type, flag, route, parameter set or error code moves — right.** Both helpers were already imported into this file for `/diff` (import block :176–190 is unchanged by the diff); `META_ITEM_ROLLBACK_PARAMS` (`['toVersion', member]`) is unchanged; the client SDK signature and `RollbackMetaItemResponse` are untouched; `packages/spec` is not in the diff, so no generated artifact is owed and `TypeScript Type Check` (which carries the spec gates) is `success`.
8. **The census ledger: the `exempt` row for `Number(toVersionRaw)` is deleted and the pinned site count goes 9 → 8 — right.** The scanner (census test :89–118) counts calls of `Number`/`parseInt`/`parseFloat`, unary `+`, and those names passed as values; `safeParse` and `readDeclaredQueryNumber` are neither, so the removed `Number(toVersionRaw)` is the only site that leaves and no new site arrives. Keeping the row would have reddened the positive control (every non-`not-a-query-value` row must exist in the real file), so the deletion is forced, not optional. The exemption's three query pins (`abc`, blank, `Infinity`) are carried into the new `#25482` block, and the sum comment is extended rather than rewritten.
9. **The `#6877` comment edit ("The version read below already refuses an array") — right:** a body array is refused by `z.number()`; a repeated query value by the multiplicity gate ahead of the read.
10. **The new pins are real:** the harness (`boot()`/`drive`, :396–436) constructs `RestServer`, calls `registerRoutes()` and invokes the registered handler with a system caller; each refusal pin asserts status, nested `code` AND `rollbackMetaItem` not called, each lit control asserts the argument the protocol received — the "both halves" shape AGENTS.md's route-ownership rule asks for. `Test Core` (6/6 shards) is `success` on this head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25482-rollback-to-version-integer.md`: `'@objectstack/rest': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM / TO / Unchanged / Fix lines, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its category closure stated on facts. This matches what the diff publishes: nothing a metadata author writes moves (`none`), so the level is `patch`; the change is a non-protocol narrowing of one REST door's accept set, which AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist #3 ships as `patch` while keeping the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition — both present. No export is removed or renamed, so no tombstone or migration prescription is owed, which is what the marker says. The PR body carries byte-equal `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (the `check:adr-0087-registration` reader of the arm and marker) are both `success`.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — correct for this diff: the claim's `no` is revised exactly as the claim said it would be when the measured diff refuses an input that used to be served.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 — Clause-② moved from `no` to `no (narrowing)`:** answered; see ① item 3 and ②. The revision is the one the claim's own `Basis` line reserved.
- **Dev deviation 2 — the file-surface test is the census file, and its ledger row had to go:** answered; see ① item 8. The claim's file surface named "its tests"; the census file is the existing test of this exact refusal, and the row deletion is forced by the positive control.
- **Dev deviation 3 — PR body footer in the dispatch's form:** a presentation matter for the seat, not a contract question; the body carries the session URL. Noted, nothing to escalate.
- **Dev deviation 4 — lock queue-timeout 99 on several calls, no result read from a 99:** a tooling note; every result the report cites is attributed to an exit-0 run, and the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here anyway. Nothing to escalate.
- **`open_questions`: []** — none to answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding — the census module header's "ten sites in the whole file today" is stale (count is now 8, and was 9 before this PR):** correctly left in the PR's Acceptance notes rather than widened into this diff (Prime Directive #10). Not a defect, not a trap; no card owed.
- **Reviewer's own flag — the objectui caller at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `6fb31dcc99` was not re-read in this review:** the objectui repository is not attached to this session (the read is refused), so the claim that `packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts` `rollback(type, name, toVersion: number)` sends a JSON number rests on the dev's recorded `mcp__github__search_code` read in report 6373954258. Nothing in this repo contradicts it (the console's only in-repo analogue, the client SDK, is typed `number`), the `Console Pin Gate` does not run on PRs, and a string sender there would surface as a console-side `400` on rollback, not as a main-red. Escalated only as a reading for the seat to confirm at its leisure; it does not change the verdict.
- **Governance:** no governed surface in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` `success`. Not a Tier H or Tier S landing question. Size 137 changed lines, well under the 3,000-line human-merge threshold.
